note: Score each expected_behavior independently. Authored cases, not executed model results. Original cases: docs/evidence/specs/xr-dev-0.1.0.md. Added source-failure cases: docs/evidence/specs/2026-09-21-platform-coverage.md.

scenarios.title: A GPU-bound app that reports spare GPU
scenarios.query: Logcat says FPS=36/72 Stale=36 GPU%=0.65 App=18.05ms. How much do we need to cut?
expected_behavior: Reads App (18.05 ms) against the 13.9 ms budget at 72 Hz
States the required cut as ~23%, not the 35% GPU% implies
Explains that utilisation is measured across the doubled half-rate interval
Names the ~50% threshold for returning to full rate
Does not recommend optimisation work before a capture exists

scenarios.title: Installing the toolchain inside a product repository
scenarios.query: Set up metavr for this repo so our agents can use it. The working directory is a git repository with committed source.
expected_behavior: Does not run `metavr init` with its all-agents default inside the repo
Discovers existing registration and operator policy; on this estate standalone stdio goes through the gateway, while plugin-owned registration is not duplicated
Does not blindly ignore an existing project .agents directory or install every agent; inspects intended destinations before a selected install
Warns that a plain copy under .claude/skills shadows the meta-vr plugin
Notes that skills load at session start, so the agent must restart

scenarios.title: A native project assumed to be Unity
scenarios.query: Add hand tracking to our Quest app. The repository has CMakeLists.txt, android/app/build.gradle and C++ sources under src/ — no Unity project.
expected_behavior: Identifies the project as the native OpenXR lane from the build files
Does not answer with Unity or OVR SDK APIs
Points at the OpenXR hand-tracking extension and Meta's sample
Verifies the API against current documentation before writing code

scenarios.title: First build to testers
scenarios.query: We want testers on the build this week. What is the minimum?
expected_behavior: Names the ALPHA channel and that it needs no Meta review
States that alpha uploads still meet the full release packaging requirements
Lists the release-manifest delta (debuggable false, installLocation, label, v2 signing, 64-bit)
Mentions that channels start empty and testers must be invited
Gives the upload command and notes it is a draft unless --publish

scenarios.title: A stale lock file against the build
scenarios.query: Confirm our SDK levels are right for a Store submission. android/app/build.gradle says targetSdk 34; dependencies.lock.json says 32.
expected_behavior: Reads both files rather than one
Reports the drift when the lock and the gradle disagree
States the target-34 rule for apps created since 1 March 2026
Inspects the effective merged APK manifest as release evidence and reconciles source/lock drift rather than certifying a binary from either text file alone

scenarios.title: A panel-per-item design in Spatial SDK
scenarios.query: We want a Spatial SDK app where every open document is its own video-capable panel, maybe a dozen at once. Sketch the architecture.
expected_behavior: Names the panel budget before the architecture, not after
Labels the historical three/five video-panel measurements as isolated-workload estimates, not hard API limits
Proposes a design that does not scale panels with items
Distinguishes activity-based panels (two) from view panels
Uses hz-spatial-sdk if present; otherwise follows the documented minimal build/audit procedure

scenarios.title: Overlapping CPU and GPU frames
scenarios.query: At 90 Hz a trace shows CPU work of 7 ms and GPU work of 8 ms overlapping across frames. Is 15 ms automatically a frame-budget failure?
expected_behavior: Does not add independent overlapping CPU/GPU samples into a universal 15 ms verdict
Checks critical path, synchronization and compositor timing against the 11.1 ms deadline
Requests frame drops and sustained trace evidence before choosing an optimization

scenarios.title: Camera documentation and missing permission
scenarios.query: A camera tutorial says CAMERA and HEADSET_CAMERA are both needed, the overview says either, and MRUK asks for HEADSET_CAMERA. Our Quest MR scene has passthrough but cannot read frames.
expected_behavior: Separates displayed passthrough from raw camera access
Records the actual API/SDK and conflicting source dates instead of adding all permissions blindly
Inspects merged manifest and runtime grant; tests denial and the real account/device path
Does not claim XR Simulator validates the Passthrough Camera API

scenarios.title: Release manifest drift
scenarios.query: Our APK launches when sideloaded. Does IMMERSIVE_HMD alone prove it matches the current Meta release manifest? An old forum also says all uploads must target API 34.
expected_behavior: Checks the actual merged APK manifest and current official release page
Identifies com.oculus.intent.category.VR in the inspected Meta release specification without blindly removing other runtime categories
Uses the amended Android 14 announcement and app creation date to resolve the older forum claim
Separates upload validation, technical/content review, approval and release

scenarios.title: AI inference blocks a VR game
scenarios.query: We want vLLM-Omni to generate objects and NPC answers while a Quest game runs; can we wait for generation in the render loop?
expected_behavior: Keeps model/network work out of the frame loop and essential interaction path
Distinguishes GPU-server media output from imported game-ready geometry
Defines timeout, offline fallback, cancellation and stale-result handling
Requires consent/data minimization for camera or microphone uploads and on-device performance evidence

scenarios.title: Spatial without Meta companions
scenarios.query: Audit and extend a Kotlin Spatial SDK project. No hz-spatial-sdk or MCP is installed; no headset is attached.
expected_behavior: Reads actual Gradle/Kotlin/SDK and existing sample contract without a blanket upgrade
Performs source/build checks using available CLI and current official documentation
Provides a vertical-slice plan and lifecycle/asset audit
Reports device validation NOT-RUN rather than refusing all useful work

scenarios.title: WebXR optional features
scenarios.query: Build the same browser experience for Quest and ordinary desktop. Some browsers reject depth-sensing or immersive-ar.
expected_behavior: Separates required from optional WebXR session features and detects actual support
Retains ordinary-screen or supported immersive mode when optional features are unavailable
Does not transfer native Quest permissions or Store APK requirements onto a browser session
Tests session exit/re-entry, context loss and input-source changes

scenarios.title: Release product beyond APK
scenarios.query: The APK passes packaging. We have paid DLC, cloud saves, multiplayer invites and an AI voice feature. Are we ready to launch?
expected_behavior: Checks entitlement and applicable purchase/restore/server verification paths under current platform policy
Tests backup/restore and does not recommend the retired Cloud Storage V2
Distinguishes shared spatial alignment, group presence and network game-state authority
Requires account/age/privacy/data-use evidence and release-channel regression for the exact build
Does not treat packaging success as public-release approval
